title: E-I Says A
kidRule: Sometimes the long A sound has no letter A in it at all! The team E-I-G-H says long A, as in NEIGHBOR and SLEIGH, and its G and H stay quiet. In a few words, E-I does the job alone, as in REINDEER.
hint: I hear a long A sound here, but there is no letter A in it! A team that starts with E writes the sound. Do you remember the team?
reminder: The long A sound here is spelled E-I or E-I-G-H, with no letter A at all.

check.question: Which letters spell the long A sound in SLEIGH?
check.correctAnswer: The team E-I-G-H says long A, and the G and H stay quiet!
distractors: The letters A-Y, just like in play
The letter A with a magic E at the end

words.def: A person who lives next door to you or very near you.
words.sent: Our neighbor waters our plants when we are away.
words.story: This word is more than a thousand years old. In Old English it meant 'near dweller', someone who lives near you!
words.card: My *neighbor* is a horse who says *neigh* whenever I mow the lawn!

words.def: A big sled that is pulled over the snow, usually by horses.
words.sent: Two horses pulled the sleigh across the snowy field.
words.story: This word comes from the Dutch word 'slee'. Dutch families who settled in America long ago brought it with them!
words.card: The *sle*epy snowman drove his *sleigh* into a pile of pillows!

words.def: Goods that are carried from place to place by train, truck, ship, or plane.
words.sent: The long train carried freight across the country.
words.story: Some freight trains are more than a mile long, with over a hundred cars!
words.card: The *freight* train carried *eight* elephants and one tiny mouse!

words.def: A large deer with antlers that lives in cold, snowy places in the far north.
words.sent: A reindeer dug through the snow to find some moss.
words.story: Both the males and the females grow antlers. They are the only kind of deer where the females do that!
words.card: The *reindeer* held his own *rein* and drove himself to the pizza shop!

words.def: Seeming to have no heaviness at all, so that you float.
words.sent: Astronauts feel weightless as they float around the space station.
words.story: Because they are weightless, astronauts on the space station sleep in sleeping bags fastened to the wall, so they do not drift away!
words.card: The *weightless* elephant lost all his *weight* and bounced along the ceiling!

words.def: Having a very pale brown color, like sand.
words.sent: We painted the bedroom walls beige.
words.story: This is a French word. It first meant the color of sheep's wool before any dye was added!
words.card: The *beige* *be*ar blended into the sand until he sneezed!

words.def: To be heavier or more important than something else.
words.sent: The good things about a puppy outweigh the muddy paw prints.
words.story: Ants are tiny, but there are so many of them that all the ants on Earth outweigh all the wild birds and wild mammals put together!
words.card: The ants *outweigh* the elephant, so they voted him *out* of the seesaw club!

words.def: To show something new for the first time, often by taking off its cover.
words.sent: The mayor will unveil the new statue on Saturday.
words.story: When it was time to unveil the Statue of Liberty in 1886, the sculptor pulled away a huge French flag that was covering her face!
words.card: Today we *unveil* our statue of a *un*icorn eating spaghetti!

words.def: A long piece of yarn wound into a loose bundle.
words.sent: Grandma bought a skein of red yarn to knit a scarf.
words.story: A flock of geese flying across the sky is also called a skein!
words.card: The kitten tried to *sk*ate down the hall on a *skein* of yarn!

words.def: Careful watching of a place or a person, often to keep things safe.
words.sent: The museum uses cameras for surveillance at night.
words.story: This word comes from the French 'surveiller', which means to watch over!
words.card: Our hamster is under *surveillance*, and *sur*prise: he is the cookie thief!
